bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: unserialize() leaks its iconv conversion descriptors when an error unwinds mid-stream

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
When a version-3 serialization stream was written under a different
native encoding than the reader's, ReadChar() in src/main/serialize.c
translates the stream's native (unflagged) strings through iconv. It
opens up to two conversion descriptors lazily and caches them in the
R_inpstream_t (nat2nat_obj, nat2utf8_obj); R_Unserialize() closes them
only on the normal return path. Any error signalled after the first
translated string unwinds past that close and leaks the descriptors --
about 33 KB each with glibc, where the gconv step buffer dominates -- on
every failing unserialize(), readRDS(), or load() call. A truncated or
corrupted file written under a different locale therefore leaks on every
load attempt.

Reachable error paths include at least:

- InString signalling "read error" for a truncated stream,
- mkCharLenCE signalling "embedded nul in string",
- allocation failures anywhere later in the stream.

Reproducible example -- serialize two native latin1 strings, rewrite the
stream header so it claims a latin1 writer (forcing a UTF-8 reader to
translate), then truncate the stream inside the second string. Run in a
UTF-8 locale:

    x <- iconv(c("h\u00e9llo", "w\u00f6rld"), "UTF-8", "latin1")
    Encoding(x) <- "unknown"                  # write them as native strings
    s <- serialize(x, NULL)                   # header names this session's UTF-8
    len <- readBin(s[15:18], "integer", endian = "big")
    s <- c(s[1:14], writeBin(10L, raw(), endian = "big"),
           charToRaw("ISO-8859-1"), s[-(1:(18 + len))])
    unserialize(s)                            # translated: "héllo" "wörld"
    bad <- head(s, -3)                        # truncate inside the second string
    for (i in 1:2000)
        try(unserialize(bad), silent = TRUE)  # "read error" each time

Observed: every failing call leaks the descriptor opened for the
translation, and the process grows without bound. Expected: the error is
signalled and nothing is retained.

Analysis: in R_Unserialize (serialize.c, trunk r90492)

    PROTECT(ref_table = MakeReadRefTable());
    obj =  ReadItem(ref_table, stream);          /* <-- may longjmp */

    if (version == 3) {
        if (stream->nat2nat_obj && stream->nat2nat_obj != (void *)-1) {
            Riconv_close(stream->nat2nat_obj);   /* never reached on error */

The stream struct lives on the caller's C stack and is initialised fresh
by R_InitInPStream, so nothing can close the descriptors once the error
has unwound. PR#19134 reports the same shape of leak (descriptors opened
lazily, released only on normal return) in do_iconv().

Measurements: unpatched trunk (r90486; serialize.c is unchanged at
r90492), aarch64-apple-darwin25.6.0, macOS leaks with MallocStackLogging
after the loop above (2001 failing calls, counting one caught by
tryCatch):

    Process 55581: 6003 leaks for 928464 total leaked bytes.

    STACK OF 2000 INSTANCES OF 'ROOT LEAK: <malloc in iconv_open_internal>':
    1   R   iconv_open_internal + 80   sysutils.c:1359

(macOS libiconv descriptors are small; glibc's are about 33 KB each.)
Patched, same loop: 0 leaks for 0 total leaked bytes.

This was found by LeakSanitizer in the ClusterFuzzLite batch fuzzing of
unserialize() in https://github.com/r-devel/r-oss-fuzz, from a 61-byte
stream declaring ANSI_X3.4-1968 as the writer encoding and holding one
native string with a non-ASCII byte and an embedded nul, so the
translation fails and mkCharLenCE signals:

    ==2371==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks
    Direct leak of 112 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
        #1 __gconv_open
        #2 iconv_open
    Indirect leak of 32640 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
        #1 __gconv_open
    SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 32960 byte(s) leaked in 3 allocation(s).

The defect itself is independent of fuzzing.

Proposed patch: attached as unserialize-iconv-leak.diff. It closes the
descriptors from a CTXT_CCODE cleanup context around ReadItem, the idiom
do_dput / do_dump use for connections, so the unwind closes them too;
the normal path is unchanged. It is independent of the patch in PR#19157
(a different leak in the same file, non-overlapping hunks) and applies
with or without it. Verified on the patched build: translation of a
mismatched-encoding stream, an error after translation, readRDS, lazy
loading, and reg-tests-1d / reg-tests-1e behave as before.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/327,
where CI results can be seen.

Created attachment 3839
patch: close unserialize's iconv descriptors on error unwind
